title: Bayesian language-model design improved measured scFv binding
summary: An end-to-end Bayesian language-model workflow designed diverse single-chain antibody fragment libraries that were measured for binding. In the 2023 journal version, the best generated scFv bound 28.7-fold better than the best directed-evolution comparator, and 99% of designs in the most successful library improved on the initial candidate. The 2022 bioRxiv v1 abstract already reported this result chain, giving 28.8-fold for the best generated scFv; the small difference is version-specific. These are in-vitro binding results, not clinical efficacy.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization with a language-model-based antibody sequence representation
organization: Massachusetts Institute of Technology Lincoln Laboratory; A-Alpha Bio, Inc.

source_review.scope: Official bioRxiv API v1 date/abstract and primary Nature journal PDF for full result and affiliations.

evidence.tested: Designed scFvs were empirically measured. The publisher abstract reports the best generated scFv had 28.7-fold greater binding than the best directed-evolution scFv and 99% of the designed scFvs in the most successful library improved on the initial candidate.
evidence.unknown: The journal version reports the best generated scFv at 28.7-fold better binding while the v1 abstract reports 28.8-fold; this minor version discrepancy is retained. The measured binding result does not establish clinical efficacy.
evidence.ai_role: A Bayesian, language-model-based workflow designed candidate scFv libraries, whose binding was experimentally measured.
